column1: haryana-history-rakhigarhi/Archaeology|Which archaeological site in Haryana is associated with the Harappan civilization?|Rakhigarhi|Sanchi|Hampi|Ajanta|Rakhigarhi is a Harappan site in Haryana. Learn archaeological evidence separately from later literary traditions.

haryana-history-rakhigarhi/Archaeology|Which other Harappan site is located in Haryana?|Banawali|Konark|Ellora|Mamallapuram|Banawali is a Harappan archaeological site in Haryana; the other places are known for later monuments.

haryana-history-rakhigarhi/History|Thanesar is closely associated with which early medieval ruler?|Harshavardhana|Alauddin Khalji|Shah Jahan|Ranjit Singh|Thanesar was an important centre associated with Harshavardhana before his later association with Kannauj.

haryana-history-rakhigarhi/History|Who wrote the Harshacharita?|Banabhatta|Kalidasa|Megasthenes|Al-Biruni|Banabhatta composed the Harshacharita. A court biography should be interpreted with attention to its context and purpose.

haryana-history-rakhigarhi/History|The First Battle of Panipat in 1526 was fought between whom?|Babur and Ibrahim Lodi|Akbar and Hemu|Marathas and Ahmad Shah Abdali|Prithviraj and Muhammad Ghori|The 1526 battle defeated Ibrahim Lodi and helped establish Mughal rule. Do not confuse the three major Panipat battles.

haryana-history-rakhigarhi/History|The Second Battle of Panipat in 1556 involved the Mughal forces and whom?|Hemu|Ibrahim Lodi|Ahmad Shah Abdali|Maharana Pratap|Hemu faced the Mughal forces during Akbar's early reign. The battle is distinct from Haldighati in 1576.

haryana-history-rakhigarhi/History|The Third Battle of Panipat took place in which year?|1761|1526|1556|1857|The third major battle was fought in 1761 between the Marathas and Ahmad Shah Abdali's forces.

haryana-history-rakhigarhi/State formation|Haryana became a separate state on which date?|1 November 1966|15 August 1947|26 January 1950|1 November 1956|Haryana was formed through the reorganization of Punjab in 1966. State formation dates are distinct from independence and Republic Day.

haryana-geography-rivers/Rivers|Which major river forms much of Haryana's eastern boundary with Uttar Pradesh?|Yamuna|Narmada|Godavari|Kaveri|The Yamuna is an important eastern boundary river. Trace rivers on a map rather than memorizing names without locations.

haryana-geography-rivers/Rivers|Which river in northern Haryana is mainly seasonal?|Ghaggar|Brahmaputra|Ganga|Godavari|The Ghaggar is a seasonal river system; its discharge differs from major perennial Himalayan rivers.

haryana-geography-rivers/Relief|Which hill system occurs in northeastern Haryana?|Shivalik|Nilgiri|Cardamom Hills|Eastern Ghats|The Shivalik foothills occur in the northeastern part of Haryana. Regional relief influences drainage and land use.

haryana-geography-rivers/Relief|Which ancient hill range extends into southern Haryana?|Aravalli|Himalayan Greater Range|Western Ghats|Patkai|The Aravalli range extends into southern Haryana and adjoining Rajasthan and Delhi.

haryana-geography-rivers/Agriculture|What is a major risk of sustained groundwater extraction exceeding recharge?|A falling groundwater table|Guaranteed unlimited water|Immediate creation of glaciers|Permanent elimination of drought|Extraction above recharge depletes groundwater. Rainfall, recharge, cropping and irrigation choices affect the balance.

haryana-geography-rivers/Agriculture|Why is a state's total annual rainfall insufficient to judge irrigation needs?|Seasonal distribution and crop water needs also matter|All crops require exactly the same water|Soil has no effect|Rain always falls uniformly|Timing, reliability, soil moisture and crop requirements matter as well as total rainfall.

haryana-geography-rivers/Climate|Which practice can reduce soil erosion on cultivated land?|Maintaining protective plant cover|Leaving every slope bare|Removing all field boundaries|Overgrazing the same land|Vegetation reduces raindrop impact and surface runoff; measures should fit local land conditions.
haryana-geography-rivers/Maps|On a conventional north-up map, which direction lies to the right?|East|West|North|South|Read the map's orientation first. With north at the top, east is on the right.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Crops|Wheat is mainly grown in which cropping season in northern India?|Rabi|Kharif|Only the monsoon harvest season|A season unrelated to temperature|Wheat is typically a rabi crop, sown in the cooler season and harvested in spring.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Crops|Rice is commonly associated with which cropping season in northern India?|Kharif|Rabi only|Only the coldest winter weeks|No seasonal pattern|Rice is commonly a kharif crop. Irrigation, varieties and local schedules can modify the calendar.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Institutions|Where is the National Dairy Research Institute located?|Karnal|Jaipur|Panaji|Shillong|NDRI is located in Karnal, Haryana; distinguish dairy research from general crop research institutions.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Institutions|Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University is located in which city?|Hisar|Kochi|Agartala|Mysuru|CCS Haryana Agricultural University is in Hisar. Learn institutions together with their field of work.
haryana-agri-husbandry/Institutions|Where is the Central Institute for Research on Buffaloes located?|Hisar|Pune|Guwahati|Bhopal|CIRB is located in Hisar and works on buffalo research.
haryana-agri-husbandry/Livestock|Murrah is a breed of which animal?|Buffalo|Sheep|Goat|Horse|Murrah is a buffalo breed associated with dairy production. It is not a cattle breed.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Livestock|Hariana is a breed of which livestock group?|Cattle|Buffalo|Poultry|Camel|Hariana is a cattle breed; similar-sounding geographic and breed names should not be confused.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Agronomy|What is crop rotation?|Growing different crops in a planned sequence on the same land|Turning harvested grain physically|Growing only one crop indefinitely|Replacing soil every week|Rotation can change nutrient demands, pest cycles and soil cover; suitable sequences depend on local conditions.

delhi-historical-heritage/Early Delhi|Lal Kot is associated with which dynasty?|Tomaras|Cholas|Pandyas|Satavahanas|Lal Kot is associated with the Tomaras and early medieval Delhi; separate archaeological history from legendary narratives.

delhi-historical-heritage/Sultanate|Who began construction of the Qutb Minar?|Qutb-ud-din Aibak|Shah Jahan|Sher Shah Suri|Akbar|Aibak began the Qutb Minar; later rulers, including Iltutmish, added to it. A monument can have multiple construction phases.
delhi-historical-heritage/Sultanate|Siri is associated with which Delhi Sultan?|Alauddin Khalji|Ibrahim Lodi|Muhammad Shah|Bahadur Shah II|Siri was a fortified city associated with Alauddin Khalji.

delhi-historical-heritage/Sultanate|Tughlaqabad is associated with which ruler?|Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq|Babur|Shah Jahan|Razia Sultan|Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq founded Tughlaqabad. Distinguish the rulers within the Tughlaq dynasty.

delhi-historical-heritage/Mughal Delhi|Who founded Shahjahanabad?|Shah Jahan|Aurangzeb|Akbar|Humayun|Shahjahanabad was built under Shah Jahan and includes major Mughal monuments such as the Red Fort and Jama Masjid.

delhi-historical-heritage/Mughal Delhi|Which river lies near Delhi's Red Fort?|Yamuna|Narmada|Mahanadi|Tapi|The Red Fort stands near the Yamuna; historic settlement and defensive choices often reflect river geography.

delhi-historical-heritage/Capital|In which year was the transfer of the British Indian capital from Calcutta to Delhi announced?|1911|1857|1931|1947|The announcement was made at the Delhi Durbar in 1911. The inauguration of New Delhi occurred later, in 1931.

delhi-historical-heritage/Capital|In which year was New Delhi formally inaugurated?|1931|1911|1905|1950|New Delhi was inaugurated in 1931; distinguish this event from the 1911 announcement of the capital transfer.

delhi-historical-heritage/Architecture|Which architects are associated with planning imperial New Delhi?|Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker|Le Corbusier and Pierre Jeanneret|Frank Lloyd Wright and Louis Sullivan|Charles Correa and Laurie Baker|Lutyens and Herbert Baker were central to the design of imperial New Delhi; Le Corbusier is associated with Chandigarh.

delhi-historical-heritage/Civics|Which constitutional article gives special provisions for the National Capital Territory of Delhi?|Article 239AA|Article 32|Article 110|Article 368|Article 239AA provides the special constitutional arrangement for Delhi; current legal details require checking authoritative texts and judgments.

army-military-heritage/Ranks|Which Army rank corresponds broadly to Navy Lieutenant and Air Force Flight Lieutenant?|Captain|Colonel|Major General|Field Marshal|Captain, Lieutenant and Flight Lieutenant are equivalent commissioned-rank levels across the three services.

army-military-heritage/Ranks|Which Army rank corresponds broadly to Navy Lieutenant Commander and Air Force Squadron Leader?|Major|Lieutenant|Brigadier|General|Major, Lieutenant Commander and Squadron Leader are equivalent commissioned-rank levels.

army-military-heritage/Ranks|Which Army rank corresponds broadly to Navy Commander and Air Force Wing Commander?|Lieutenant Colonel|Captain|Major General|Lieutenant|Lieutenant Colonel, Commander and Wing Commander form the corresponding level.

army-military-heritage/Ranks|Which Army rank corresponds broadly to Navy Captain and Air Force Group Captain?|Colonel|Major|Lieutenant|Brigadier|Colonel, Captain and Group Captain are equivalent commissioned-rank levels; the word Captain denotes different levels in Army and Navy.

army-military-heritage/Honours|What is India's highest wartime gallantry award?|Param Vir Chakra|Ashoka Chakra|Kirti Chakra|Shaurya Chakra|The Param Vir Chakra is the highest wartime gallantry award; the Ashoka Chakra is the highest peacetime gallantry award.

army-military-heritage/Honours|What is India's highest peacetime gallantry award?|Ashoka Chakra|Vir Chakra|Maha Vir Chakra|Param Vir Chakra|The Ashoka Chakra recognizes exceptional gallantry outside the wartime award category.

army-military-heritage/Honours|Who was the first recipient of the Param Vir Chakra?|Major Somnath Sharma|Captain Vikram Batra|Field Marshal Sam Manekshaw|Marshal Arjan Singh|Major Somnath Sharma was the first recipient, for his gallantry during the 1947 conflict.
army-military-heritage/Operations|Operation Meghdoot is associated with which area?|Siachen|Goa|Hyderabad|Andaman Islands|Operation Meghdoot in 1984 is associated with the Siachen area.

army-military-heritage/Operations|Operation Polo in 1948 is associated with which former princely state?|Hyderabad|Junagadh|Mysore|Travancore|Operation Polo was the military action associated with the integration of Hyderabad in 1948.

army-military-heritage/Operations|Operation Vijay in 1961 is associated with which territory?|Goa|Siachen|Kargil|Hyderabad|Operation Vijay was used for the 1961 Goa operation and also for the 1999 Kargil operation; the year is essential.

army-military-heritage/Operations|Operation Vijay in 1999 is associated with which conflict?|Kargil|The 1961 Goa operation|Operation Polo|The First Anglo-Sikh War|The 1999 use of Operation Vijay refers to Kargil. An operation name alone can be ambiguous without its date.

army-military-heritage/Services|Which service principally conducts naval operations?|Indian Navy|Indian Army|Indian Air Force|Indian Coast Guard as the only naval service|The Navy is the naval branch of the armed forces; the Coast Guard has distinct maritime law-enforcement and safety roles.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Agronomy|What is the main purpose of preparing a seedbed?|Create suitable conditions for seed placement, germination and root establishment|Remove every soil organism|Make irrigation permanently unnecessary|Replace every nutrient with sand|Seedbed preparation manages soil structure, weeds and seed contact; excessive disturbance can also damage soil, so methods depend on conditions.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Agronomy|Why is appropriate sowing depth important?|It affects moisture access, emergence and seedling establishment|Every seed must be buried at the same depth|Deeper sowing always guarantees higher yield|Seed depth changes the crop's species|Depth should suit seed size, soil texture and moisture rather than follow one universal value.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Agronomy|What does seed germination percentage express?|The proportion of tested seeds that germinate under the stated test conditions|The number of leaves on every mature plant|The proportion of rainfall converted into milk|The percentage of stones in soil|Germination tests estimate viable establishment potential under specified conditions; field emergence can differ.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Agronomy|In a test of 100 seeds, 85 germinate. What is the germination percentage?|85 percent|15 percent|1.18 percent|185 percent|Germination percentage is germinated seeds divided by tested seeds times 100: 85 ÷ 100 × 100 = 85 percent.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Agronomy|Why should crop spacing be appropriate for the crop and conditions?|It affects competition for light, water and nutrients|Closer spacing always gives unlimited yield|Spacing makes soil fertility irrelevant|Plants never compete for resources|Population density influences growth and yield; both overcrowding and excessively sparse stands can reduce performance.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Agronomy|What is intercropping?|Growing two or more crops together in a planned spatial arrangement|Growing one crop repeatedly for every season|Only changing a tractor's tyres|Harvesting the same crop twice per hour|Intercropping differs from a sequence of crops over time; crop combinations and arrangements must be chosen appropriately.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Agronomy|What is a weed in crop production?|A plant growing where it is unwanted in the managed crop|Every plant with green leaves|Only a crop's harvested grain|Any plant that can photosynthesize|Weed status depends on context; weeds can compete with the intended crop for resources.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Agronomy|Why is early weed control often important?|Young crops can be especially vulnerable to resource competition|Weeds always increase crop yield|All weeds disappear at sowing|Weeds cannot use water|Control during critical competition periods can protect establishment; timing and method depend on crop and weed ecology.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Soil|Which soil fraction generally has the smallest mineral particles?|Clay|Sand|Gravel|Pebbles|Clay particles are finer than silt and sand, affecting water retention, aeration and nutrient interactions.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Soil|What does soil texture describe?|The relative proportions of sand, silt and clay|Only the soil's temperature at noon|Only the number of earthworms|The colour of harvested grain|Texture refers to particle-size composition and influences physical behaviour; it differs from soil structure.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Soil|What does soil structure describe?|How soil particles are organized into aggregates|Only the number of crop varieties|Only a field's boundary length|Only dissolved fertilizer colour|Aggregation creates pores that influence water movement, aeration and root growth.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Soil|Why can soil organic matter support crop production?|It contributes to aggregation, nutrient cycling and water retention|It eliminates every crop disease permanently|It makes sunlight unnecessary|It converts all sand directly into clay|Organic matter supports several soil functions, but results depend on its amount, quality and management.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Soil|What is soil erosion?|Removal and movement of soil by agents such as water or wind|Formation of every new root|Increase in grain protein only|Storage of milk in a tank|Erosion can remove fertile topsoil and transport sediment; ground cover and appropriate management can reduce exposure.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Soil|Which practice can help reduce wind erosion on exposed farmland?|Maintaining suitable cover and windbreaks|Leaving all soil bare indefinitely|Removing every boundary plant|Increasing exposure to strong winds|Vegetation and shelter reduce near-surface wind effects; design should suit the landscape and farm operations.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Soil|What is salinity in agricultural soil?|An accumulation of soluble salts that can affect plant growth|The complete absence of all mineral ions|Only a high population of insects|A synonym for seed maturity|Excess salts can limit water uptake and cause other stress; diagnosis and management require site-specific information.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Nutrition|What do N, P and K denote on common fertilizer labels?|Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium|Nickel, platinum and krypton|Neon, polonium and calcium|Sodium, phosphorus and iron|NPK identifies three major plant nutrients; label conventions for reporting phosphorus and potassium should be read carefully.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Nutrition|Why is soil testing useful before deciding fertilizer inputs?|It informs nutrient status and more appropriate input planning|It guarantees maximum yield regardless of weather|It replaces all crop observation|It removes the need to know the crop|A test is one input to nutrient management along with crop requirements, soil conditions and previous management.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Nutrition|Which biological process allows suitable legume-root associations to add usable nitrogen to the system?|Nitrogen fixation by symbiotic bacteria|Conversion of all oxygen into nitrogen by leaves|Melting of root minerals|Evaporation of fertilizer bags|Symbiotic bacteria in suitable legume nodules can fix atmospheric nitrogen; effectiveness depends on the plant, bacteria and conditions.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Nutrition|Why should fertilizer placement and timing match crop demand?|They can improve nutrient use and reduce avoidable losses|All fertilizer is equally effective at every time|Plants absorb nutrients only after harvest|Timing changes soil into a different element|Nutrient availability should coincide with uptake while considering rainfall, irrigation and loss pathways.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Nutrition|What is composting?|Managed biological decomposition of organic material|Mixing diesel with irrigation water|Turning every mineral into a gas|Freezing fresh grain without change|Composting uses organisms to stabilize organic material under suitable moisture, aeration and feedstock conditions.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Water|What is irrigation?|Supplying water to crops through managed means|Only rain falling naturally|Only storing harvested grain|Removing all roots from soil|Irrigation supplements water availability; suitable timing and amounts depend on crop stage, soil and weather.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Water|Why can over-irrigation be harmful?|It can cause waterlogging, nutrient loss and poor root aeration|It always doubles available oxygen in soil|It makes drainage unnecessary|It prevents every pest|Excess water can fill pore space and limit oxygen; effects vary with soil and drainage.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Water|What is drip irrigation mainly designed to do?|Deliver water locally near the plant root zone|Flood every field to unlimited depth|Spray only the road outside the farm|Remove the crop's need for roots|Drip systems apply water through emitters; proper operation requires design, filtration and maintenance.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Water|What is the main function of field drainage?|Remove excess water and support suitable root-zone conditions|Keep every field permanently flooded|Increase salt inputs deliberately|Prevent all rainfall from reaching plants|Drainage manages excess water; the appropriate system depends on terrain, soil and environmental considerations.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Water|Why can mulching help conserve soil moisture?|It reduces exposed-surface evaporation and can moderate conditions|It creates water from nothing|It eliminates every irrigation requirement|It makes roots absorb only air|A suitable mulch covers the surface and changes evaporation and temperature; benefits and risks depend on material and setting.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Protection|What is integrated pest management?|Combining monitoring and suitable preventive, biological, cultural and other controls|Using the strongest chemical on every field daily|Ignoring pest identity|Removing all beneficial organisms|IPM uses evidence and multiple tools to manage pest damage while considering economic and environmental effects.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Protection|Why should a crop pest be identified before choosing a control?|Different pests and life stages require different responses|Every insect is the same pest|All insects damage crops equally|Pest identity changes fertilizer colour|Correct diagnosis helps avoid ineffective or unnecessary actions and protects beneficial organisms.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Protection|What is one benefit of monitoring fields regularly?|Detect emerging problems and guide timely decisions|Guarantee that weather never changes|Replace the need for any evidence|Eliminate all labour permanently|Observation helps identify pests, deficiencies and water stress before making management decisions.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Harvest|Why is harvest timing important?|It influences yield recovery, quality and storage performance|All crops mature on the same date|Late harvest always eliminates every loss|Harvest timing changes the crop's chromosome count|The appropriate stage depends on crop and intended use; excessively early or delayed harvest can cause losses.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Harvest|Why should grain be dried appropriately before storage?|Excess moisture can encourage deterioration and mould|Wet grain never spoils|Drying always destroys every seed|Moisture has no effect on storage|Safe storage conditions depend on grain type, moisture, temperature and duration; drying is a key part of management.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Harvest|Why are clean storage structures useful?|They reduce sources of contamination and stored-product pests|They make every grain nutritionally identical|They remove the need to manage moisture|They turn grain into fertilizer automatically|Cleaning and maintenance complement moisture control and monitoring rather than replace them.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Livestock|What distinguishes a breed from a species in animal husbandry?|A breed is a selected population within a species with associated traits|Every breed is a different biological kingdom|Breed always means only the animal's age|Species is another word for a feed bag|Breeds are populations shaped by selection and history within a species; variation still occurs among individuals.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Livestock|What is a ration in livestock feeding?|The feed allowance provided over a stated period, commonly a day|Only the animal's ear tag|Only the farm boundary|The number of wheels on a milk tanker|A ration is planned to meet an animal's nutritional needs for its stage and production level.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Livestock|Why should a livestock ration be balanced?|Energy, protein, fibre, minerals and other needs must be considered together|One nutrient alone replaces all others|Every animal needs identical feed quantities|Water is never needed|Requirements differ with species, age, body size and production; balance concerns the whole diet.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Livestock|Which material is a roughage feed?|Dry fodder rich in structural fibre|A steel bucket|Pure common salt only|A plastic ear tag|Roughages provide substantial fibre; concentrates generally contain less fibre and more concentrated nutrients.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Livestock|Why is access to clean drinking water important for farm animals?|Water supports normal body functions and feed use|It replaces every nutrient permanently|It is required only once at birth|It eliminates every housing need|Water needs vary with size, feed, temperature and production, making reliable clean access important.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Livestock|Why should livestock housing have suitable ventilation?|It helps manage heat, moisture and air quality|It removes all need for shelter|It guarantees zero pathogens|It prevents every weather event|Ventilation is one part of housing management alongside shade, space, cleanliness and protection from unsuitable conditions.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Livestock|What is the main purpose of keeping animal production records?|Track performance and inform management decisions|Replace the animal's identity with a guess|Make all animals produce identical amounts|Avoid knowing feed costs|Records of identity, production, feeding and other events support comparison and planning.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Dairy|Why is hygiene important during milking and handling milk?|It reduces avoidable contamination|It turns milk into a mineral|It eliminates the need for clean equipment|It makes temperature irrelevant|Clean handling limits contamination, while appropriate cooling and storage are additional requirements.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Dairy|What does pasteurization of milk primarily involve?|A controlled heat treatment to reduce harmful microorganisms|Removing every protein from milk|Adding soil to improve flavour|Converting milk directly into a metal|Pasteurization uses a specified time-temperature process; it does not make storage practices unnecessary or sterilize every product.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Dairy|Why is prompt appropriate cooling of collected milk useful?|It slows microbial growth during storage|It guarantees unlimited storage life|It increases the number of harmful microbes deliberately|It removes every dissolved nutrient|Cooling helps preserve quality alongside hygiene; it does not reverse contamination or remove the need for safe handling.

haryana-agri-husbandry/Farm accounting|A farmer sells 200 kg of produce at 25 rupees per kg. What is gross sales revenue?|5000 rupees|225 rupees|8 rupees|175 rupees|Revenue is quantity times price: 200 × 25 = 5000 rupees, before subtracting costs.
